title: Kale, apple and carrot slaw with toasted seeds

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Kale, carrots, apples, seeds, natural yoghurt, mustard, honey and lemon are all plain home staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco or any mainstream supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, a bowl, a grater and a knife, and the technique is simple massaging and grating.

works.reason: 200g kale, two carrots and two apples with a four-tablespoon yoghurt dressing is a sensible amount for four snack portions, and massaging the kale with oil and salt makes it pleasant to eat raw.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers stripping and shredding the kale, massaging it, grating the carrots and apples and mixing the dressing, and five minutes suits toasting the seeds.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon, salt and pepper, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Kale is the bulk and point of the slaw, and a crunchy winter slaw of kale, apple and carrot suits early December.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a satisfying snack of vegetables, fruit, seeds and yoghurt with only a teaspoon of honey.
